transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer retentions, my name is Jessica. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Jessica. I am calling because my latest broadband bill jumped from forty-two pounds a month to seventy-nine pounds without warning! I have been a loyal customer for five years, and it feels like long-standing customers are penalized while new customers get massive promotional discounts!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how frustrating it is when an eighteen-month promotional discount expires and your monthly bill increases unexpectedly, David. Let me look into our available retention tariff options for you immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Jessica. Paying seventy-nine pounds for broadband is completely out of the question on my fixed state pension when heating and council tax bills are rising every April.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open your subscription profile and current package bundle on our retentions portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our current package is the Superfast 150 fiber broadband with the weekend landline calls add-on, and my account reference number is 7701 4419.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are looking for today: your initial eighteen-month contract expired, increasing your monthly charge from forty-two pounds to seventy-nine pounds, and you want to renegotiate a competitive renewal rate comparable to alternative fiber providers. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly that. If S-Net cannot offer a competitive rate around forty pounds, I will have no choice but to switch our home services to another broadband provider on our street.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at your account, your previous eighteen-month contract included a thirty-seven pound monthly promotional credit that concluded in September.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why doesn't S-Net automatically notify customers before promotional discounts expire so we don't get hit with massive bill shock?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated billing platform prints a reminder notification across the final two monthly invoices prior to discount expiration.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I receive paperless e-billing, and the email notification just says 'Your monthly bill is ready to view' without highlighting that the price is doubling!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The full PDF statement available on the customer portal details the promotional expiration schedule.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Other competitor providers in our street like Community Fibre and Vodafone are offering nine hundred megabits for thirty-five pounds a month on a two-year contract, and they throw in free installation!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alternative alt-net fiber providers often advertise introductory loss-leader rates that increase significantly upon mid-contract annual price rises, and their customer service centers are often based overseas.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Even so, thirty-five pounds is less than half of what S-Net is currently trying to charge me for a much slower speed tier!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me on hold for about thirty-five seconds while I query our retentions discount matrix for eligible loyalty tariffs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, David. I have accessed our specialized customer retention offers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the best price you can offer to keep my custom?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can offer you our standard renewal tariff on Superfast 150 at sixty-two pounds per month on an eighteen-month contract.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sixty-two pounds?! That is still twenty pounds a month more than I was paying last month, and nearly double what competitors charge!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sixty-two pounds represents a substantial seventeen-pound monthly discount off standard out-of-contract book pricing, which is the maximum available on standard retail systems.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am telling you that Vodafone is offering three times that speed for thirty-five pounds! Why should I pay sixty-two pounds for old technology?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well Mr. David, if you want cheap budget broadband from a budget provider with zero customer service, you're welcome to leave, nobody is forcing you to stay with S-Net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is absolutely no need to be rude and insulting! I have paid S-Net thousands of pounds over five years, and telling a customer to leave is shockingly unprofessional!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I apologize if my remark was perceived as impolite, David. I am merely stating that premium optical networks command higher market value than discount providers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I want to speak to a retentions supervisor who values customer loyalty.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As a senior retentions executive, I have full discretionary authority to access our tier three legacy preservation credits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then why didn't you offer that in the first place instead of insulting me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Tier three discretionary credits require senior manager validation based on account tenure and payment history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the tier three preservation offer look like?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can upgrade your broadband to Gigafast 500 at forty-four pounds per month fixed for twenty-four months with zero mid-contract CPI price hikes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Forty-four pounds for five hundred megabits with complete price protection against inflation?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that includes a speed upgrade from one hundred and fifty megabits to five hundred megabits, an upgraded Hub 5 router, and guaranteed price protection against April retail price index increases.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that forty-four pounds include line rental and our weekend evening calls package?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the digital voice line rental and unlimited weekend calls to UK landlines and mobiles are fully included within the forty-four pound monthly fee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is significantly closer to what I was hoping for, and the extra speed will be useful when our grandchildren visit to stream movies.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also waive the standard thirty-five pound router delivery fee and contract renewal administration charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Waiving the administration fee is very fair and appreciated, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In addition, I will apply a one-off thirty-five pound billing credit to offset the higher charge you experienced on this month's seventy-nine pound bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Refunding the seventy-nine pound overcharge makes me feel much more respected as a loyal five-year customer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, David, your account reference number is 7701 4419?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have locked that twenty-four month promotional price plan under reference RET-44819-D.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me note down that reference... RET-44819-D.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new contract terms and pre-contract summary information sheet have been dispatched to your registered email address.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will check that email summary on my tablet this evening.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The contract includes a fourteen-day statutory cooling-off period during which you can cancel without any exit penalties if you change your mind.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Having a fourteen-day cooling-off buffer gives good peace of mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How is your current router Wi-Fi signal performing across your property?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Wi-Fi signal has always been very reliable across our bungalow, we get full coverage in the garden too, so physical stability has never been an issue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new Hub 5 will deliver even stronger Wi-Fi 6 beamforming across your bungalow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will be an added bonus.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Jessica, does this new contract require a technician to visit or does the router arrive by courier?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new Hub 5 arrives by Royal Mail Special Delivery tracked post within forty-eight hours and is simple plug-and-play self-installation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And does my existing cordless landline telephone plug directly into the new Hub 5 green phone adapter socket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the router packaging includes the green RJ11 digital voice adapter and step-by-step setup instructions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Jessica, my daughter lives in Toronto, Canada, so does that forty-four pound price include our international calling bolt-on or is that separate...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The package is confirmed at forty-four pounds. Have a good day. Thank you for choosing S-Net, David. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Jessica, what about international calls... hello?
